nodes.name: Microwave-assisted shock synthesis of Ru_x(Ir,Fe,Co,Ni)_{1-x} series
nodes.procedure: Ru_x(Ir,Fe,Co,Ni)_{1-x} nanoparticles were synthesized using the microwave-assisted shock synthesis method on carbon paper substrates with various x atomic percentages (x = 0, 0.08, 0.12, 0.16, 0.20 at.%) following our previously reported procedure (see the Methods section in the Supporting Information for details). The 3d metal components (M = Fe, Co, Ni) were purposely selected since the bimetallic combinations of RuM or IrM have been reported to exhibit enhanced OER activity and stability.
nodes.source_text: Ru_x(Ir,Fe,Co,Ni)_{1-x} nanoparticles were synthesized using the microwave-assisted shock synthesis method on carbon paper substrates with various x atomic percentages (x = 0,0.08,0.12,0.16,0.20 at.%) following our previously reported procedure...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru_x(Ir,Fe,Co,Ni)_{1-x} shows multiphase structures at near-equimolar Ru concentrations with major fcc phase (a_fcc = 0.368 nm) and minor hcp phase (a_hcp = 0.262 nm, c_hcp = 0.424 nm) for Ru_{0.20}(Ir,Fe,Co,Ni)_{0.80}. IrFeCoNi assumes single-phase fcc structure with a = 0.365 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1a depicts the powder X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns of all Ru_x(Ir,Fe,Co,Ni)_{1-x} variations. IrFeCoNi assumed a typical face-centered cubic (fcc) crystal structure with an average lattice constant of 0.365 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: HR-STEM confirms fcc phase from fcc-[111] zone axis and hcp phase from hcp-[1213] zone axis in Ru_{0.20}(Ir,Fe,Co,Ni)_{0.80} nanoparticles with random elemental distribution visible from Z-contrast.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1b depicts the lattice structure and the corresponding fast Fourier transform (FFT) analysis of the fcc phase in Ru_{0.20}(Ir,Fe,Co,Ni)_{0.80} as seen from the fcc-[111] zone axis.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM shows well-dispersed nanoparticles (5-150 nm) on carbon paper substrate.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A low magnification HAADF-STEM image shows the dispersion of nanoparticles on a carbon paper substrate (scale bar: 200 nm).

nodes.characterization_summary: STEM-EDS maps show homogeneous distribution of Ru, Ir, Fe, Co, Ni elements in Ru_{0.20}(Ir,Fe,Co,Ni)_{0.80} nanoparticles without apparent phase separation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1e depicts the STEM-EDS maps of each element in Ru_{0.20}(Ir,Fe,Co,Ni)_{0.80}, showing the homogeneity of the synthesized nanoparticles without apparent phase separation.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES confirms atomic ratios of all variations close to nominal values.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The atomic ratio of all variations was evaluated to be close to the nominal value, as determined by STEM-EDS (local) and inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES, whole sample).

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution XPS of post-electrolyzed Ru_{0.20}(Ir,Fe,Co,Ni)_{0.80} shows positive shifts in Ru 3d_{5/2}, Ir 4f_{7/2/5/2}, and O 1s peaks indicating surface oxidation and formation of amorphous RuO_x/IrO_x shell layer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: With respect to the as-prepared sample, the postelectrolyzed catalyst shows consistent positive shifts due to the increased spectral contribution of the species with higher oxidation states, indicating the oxidation of the catalyst after undergoing OER, as demonstrated by Ru 3d_{5/2} peak (Figure 4f), as well as Ir 4f_{7/2} and Ir 4f_{5/2} peaks (Figure 4g).

nodes.characterization_summary: HR-TEM images confirm presence of multiphase fcc and hcp structures in as-prepared Ru_{0.20}(Ir,Fe,Co,Ni)_{0.80}.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figures S6 and S7 show additional lattice structure analysis from HAADF-STEM and high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HR-TEM) images of as-prepared Ru_{0.20}(Ir,Fe,Co,Ni)_{0.80}, respectively, further confirming the presence of the multiphase structures.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-electrolysis STEM-EDS shows homogeneous elemental distribution in nanoparticle core with RuIr-rich oxide shell layer (1-3 nm thick) and 3d metal depletion near surface in Ru_{0.20}(Ir,Fe,Co,Ni)_{0.80}.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From STEM-EDS elemental and composite maps displayed in Figure 4a, the dissolution of the 3d metals induces the development of a thin RuIr-rich shell layer near the surface of the evolved nanoparticles while the core maintains the homogeneous distribution of all five elements.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-electrolysis HAADF-STEM reveals 1-2 nm thick amorphous RuIr-rich oxide shell layer over pristine fcc core in evolved Ru_{0.20}(Ir,Fe,Co,Ni)_{0.80} nanoparticles; shell thickness stable after 24h operation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 4d and S20 show the thin shell layer formed on the surface of the evolved nanoparticles after the electrochemical activation step. The average thickness of the shell layer was also ~1-2 nm consistent with the STEM-EDS line profile analysis.
